rf_gateway_unsupported.title: {name} identifies as an RF Gateway, not a PoE Shade
rf_gateway_unsupported.description:
Your device identifies as an RF Gateway, not a PoE Shade. The maintainer of hass-powershades (@vemboy200) cannot build or test this integration against RF gateways.

This can mean some entities may not work as expected, a future change could unknowingly break compatibility, and there's no support for features exclusive to RF gateways. On top of that, there's no documentation for this setup, and dynamic and stale device handling (which doesn't matter for PoE shades) isn't implemented, despite this integration claiming Platinum.

Please report your experience so this can be tracked and improved.

untrusted_server_hostname.title: {name} is not configured to talk to PowerShades' own servers

confirm.title: Reset Server Hostname
confirm.description:
Your shade's Server Hostname setting is currently "{hostname}", not "{expected}". This setting controls where the shade's own cloud-facing commands connect - including Check for Updates, the Firmware update entity, and, if Allow Cloud Connection is enabled, the official PowerShades app's remote (away-from-home) control - and it can be changed by anyone on your network, since PowerShades' protocol has no authentication for this.

If Allow Cloud Connection is on, an untrusted hostname here means remote-control commands for this shade could be going to a server that isn't PowerShades' own, not just firmware/version info.

The Firmware update entity's Install action is blocked while this is set to an untrusted value. Checking for updates still works, but its "latest version" result should not be trusted until this is corrected.

Select Submit to reset it back to PowerShades' own domain, "{expected}", or use the powershades.set_server_hostname service directly if you'd rather set a different value.
